title: Unified streaming error surface and retry guidance for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our three official SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) surface streaming APIs with different exception shapes and retry semantics. Customers building real-time features report confusion about when a streaming error is retryable, how partial results are surfaced, and how to distinguish transient infra issues from model-level errors.

Problem statement: Lack of a consistent, documented error surface leads to brittle client logic, duplicated retry implementations, and poor telemetry correlation across languages. This ticket defines a single canonical error taxonomy (codes + attributes), streaming ergonomics for partial/terminal errors, and pragmatic client-side retry guidance. The goal is not to force identical idioms across languages but to standardize: error codes, retryability buckets, metadata keys, and example patterns.

Scope:
- Define canonical error codes (e.g., INTERNAL, NETWORK_TIMEOUT, RATE_LIMIT, MODEL_REJECTED, STREAM_INCOMPLETE) and per-code retry policy (never/conditional/always).
- Design a streaming error envelope that includes: code, message, retry_after (ms), attempt_id, partial_response_present (bool), kv of diagnostics.
- Add consistent SDK primitives: a typed StreamingError (or equivalent) and helper utilities (is_retryable(err), should_backoff(err)) in each SDK.
- Provide cross-language example snippets for common patterns (automatic exponential backoff for NETWORK_TIMEOUT, fast-fail for MODEL_REJECTED, graceful consumption of partial responses).
- Instrumentation: ensure error codes and retry decisions emit standardized telemetry tags for later aggregation.
- Backwards compatibility: map previously emitted error shapes to new codes via an adapter layer in the runtime so older clients get translated messages while new clients receive the enriched envelope.

Approach:
1) Draft canonical taxonomy and streaming envelope in this ticket.
2) Collaborate with Python/TS/Go leads to design idiomatic primitives (exceptions in Python, Error subclasses in TS/Go, typed error structs for Go).
3) Implement a runtime-side mapping (server) that emits the new envelope and a temporary adapter that also mirrors legacy shapes.
4) Implement SDK changes behind feature flags and ship language-specific helpers and examples.
5) Run a short dogfood rollout with internal services and one customer pilot.

Rollout plan: runtime change -> SDK alpha releases -> internal dogfood -> public beta -> GA. Each SDK release includes migration docs and code examples.

Notes: This ticket is intentionally cross-cutting: it touches the runtime, SDKs, Console telemetry, and docs. Coordinate with Observability (for telemetry tags) and Developer Experience (for examples and docs).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical taxonomy doc exists and is approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go)
Streaming error envelope schema defined and published (fields: code, message, retry_after_ms, attempt_id, partial_response_present, diagnostics)
SDK primitives implemented in master for Python/TS/Go behind feature flags: StreamingError type and is_retryable()/should_backoff() helpers
Runtime emits new envelope and adapter for legacy clients; integration tests validate mapping for at least 6 historical error shapes
Examples and migration guide published in SDK repo README and Developer Docs with copy-paste snippets for each language
Telemetry tags added: error.code, error.retry_decision, error.attempt_id; dashboards updated to show retryable vs non-retryable errors
Dogfood rollout completed with two internal services and one external pilot with documented feedback
No user-facing breakages in canaries; rollout checklist signed off by Release Manager
